/-!
# Erdős Problem 409

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/409](https://www.erdosproblems.com/409)
-/

open scoped Topology ArithmeticFunction.sigma Nat
open Filter

namespace Erdos409

/--
How many iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ are needed before a prime is reached?
-/
-- Formalisation note: the sequence of iterates always terminates if `n > 0`
-- since it is strictly decreasing unless the input is prime, at which point
-- it becomes static. See also https://oeis.org/A39651
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- If $n > 0$, then the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ necessarily
reaches a prime. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.termination (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime := by
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    by_cases hp : n.Prime
    · exact ⟨0, by simpa using hp⟩
    · have h1 : n = 1 ∨ 1 < n := by omega
      rcases h1 with h1 | h1
      · subst h1
        refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
        norm_num [Function.iterate_one, Nat.totient_one]
      · have hlt : φ n < n := Nat.totient_lt n h1
        have hne : φ n ≠ n - 1 := by
          intro h
          exact hp ((Nat.totient_eq_iff_prime hn).1 h)
        have hdec : φ n + 1 < n := by omega
        have hpos : 0 < φ n + 1 := by positivity
        obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := ih (φ n + 1) hdec hpos
        refine ⟨i + 1, ?_⟩
        rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
        exact hi

-- Formalisation note: it's possible that solution to `erdos_409.parts.i` needs to be
-- expressed asymptotically. To handle this we include `IsTheta`, `IsBigO`
-- and `IsLittleO` variants below. Since a solution is not known this necessitates
-- the use of an `answer(sorry)` placeholder. Trivial or sub-optimal solutions
-- will therefore exist to the asymptotic formalisations. A true solution to
-- the asymptotic variants should have a degree of optimality or non-triviality to it.
/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. What is $\Theta(c(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isTheta (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = O(g(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isBigO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = o(g(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isLittleO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Can infinitely many $n$ reach the same prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
What is the density of $n$ which reach any fixed prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.iii (p : ℕ) (h : p.Prime) (α : ℝ)
    (hα : { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.HasDensity α) :
    α = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
How many iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ are needed before a prime is reached?
-/
-- Formalisation note: non-termination of this sequence is less clear since
-- it is strictly increasing except at primes.
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1) :
    IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- If $n > 1$ then the iteration $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ necessarily reaches a prime.
Note: this is open — it is not clear that the σ iteration always terminates,
since it is non-decreasing (unlike the φ iteration which is strictly decreasing). -/

    ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime := by
  sorry

-- Formalisation note: See the above formalisation note for the rationale
-- for including asymptotic variants
/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime
is reached. What is $\Theta(c(n))$?
-/

/--

is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = O(g(n))$?
-/

/--

    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by

/--
Is it true that iterates of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ always reach a prime?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_prime_termination :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos409

findings.description: Lines 114–116 assume that the basin of p already has a natural density α, rather than determining whether it has a density and what that density is. For a proposed value d, the resulting condition ∀ α, B.HasDensity α → α = d is equivalent to (¬ ∃ α, B.HasDensity α) ∨ B.HasDensity d. This equivalence was proved in the scratch file. Thus the declaration permits the density not to exist, without recording that outcome, and becomes vacuous for any such p. No other declaration supplies the missing existence assertion.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 81, asks: “What is the density of n which reach p?” The same question appears at https://www.erdosproblems.com/409 and https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/409, without an assumption that the density exists. Original book: https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/ron/papers/80_11_number_theory.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the α and hα parameters and state `{n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p}.HasDensity (answer(sorry) : ℝ)` if the intended answer includes existence of the density. If nonexistence is to remain a possible answer, use an answer type such as Option ℝ, with conditions recording both the existence/value and the nonexistence cases.

findings.description: The natural-number answer and IsLeast conclusion require a finite prime-hitting time for every n > 1. IsLeast includes membership in the set, so any answer k immediately proves that the k-th iterate is prime. Consequently this timing declaration additionally asserts universal σ-termination, rather than treating timing conditionally on termination. A negative answer to the source's termination question cannot be represented by any value of this answer slot. The scratch file proves that existence of a total minimum-hitting-time function is equivalent to universal termination.
findings.source_evidence: The original source explicitly separates the questions: “Is it true that iterates of this always eventually reach a prime? If so, how soon?” Erdős–Graham (1980), p. 81, https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/ron/papers/80_11_number_theory.pdf. This conditional wording is retained at https://www.erdosproblems.com/409. The source does not establish universal termination.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the timing theorem conditional on universal termination, for example by adding `(hterm : ∀ m > 1, ∃ i, ((σ 1 · - 1)^[i] m).Prime)`, while retaining `sigma_prime_termination` as the yes-or-no question. Alternatively use an extended or optional stopping-time answer that can represent nontermination.

findings.description: The explanatory comment at lines 33–35 says that the φ iteration is strictly decreasing for positive inputs unless the input is prime. The permitted input n = 1 is an exception: 1 is not prime, but φ(1) + 1 = 2 > 1. The stopping-time statement remains correct, and the fully proved termination variant correctly handles this exception separately.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A039651, https://oeis.org/A039651, defines the same iteration count with offset 1 and first term 1. Here φ(1) = 1, so the first trajectory is 1 → 2. This behavior was also verified directly in Lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the map strictly decreases at composite inputs greater than 1, that primes are fixed, and that 1 reaches 2 in one step.

reformulations.difference: The Lean basin includes all natural starting values, including zero, and expresses reaching p by equality at some iterate rather than eventual stabilization at p.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For prime p, φ(p) + 1 = p, so reaching p is equivalent to being constantly p from some iteration onward. Removing the single starting value zero cannot change whether a basin is infinite. The combined equivalence with positive starting values and eventual stabilization was proved as Review409.part_ii_equivalence.

reformulations.difference: The conditional timing question is represented through a function c satisfying minimum-hitting-time hypotheses, rather than an explicit universal-termination premise.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Such a c exists exactly when every orbit starting above 1 reaches a prime: use IsLeast membership in one direction and Nat.find in the other. Any two such functions agree for n > 1, so their real casts are eventually equal. For any fixed candidate g, the theorem's universally quantified conditional Θ statement is therefore equivalent to an explicit 'if universal termination holds, its stopping time has the proposed Θ bound' statement. This equivalence was proved in scratch.

reformulations.difference: The source's 'if so' qualification is encoded by assuming a total function c of minimum hitting times.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Existence of c is equivalent to universal termination, and all valid c agree above 1. Since Big-O is invariant under eventual equality, the declaration is equivalent, for each proposed comparison function, to the corresponding upper-bound assertion conditional on universal termination. The equivalence was proved as Review409.conditional_bigO_equiv.

reformulations.difference: The source's conditional timing question is expressed using hypotheses defining c, rather than an explicit termination assumption.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The count-function hypotheses are satisfiable exactly under universal termination. Minimum hitting times are unique above 1, and their arbitrary values at 0 and 1 do not affect little-o atTop. Review409.conditional_littleO_equiv proves equivalence with the explicitly conditional formulation for any fixed candidate comparison function.

sources_consulted: Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), pp. 80–82, especially p. 81: https://fanchung.ucsd.edu/ron/papers/80_11_number_theory.pdf
Local review guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and AGENTS.md at the supplied checkout.
Local calibration: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr00056.md, pr01155.md, pr01406.md, pr04290.md, pr04731.md, pr05060.md.

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Set/Density.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and AnswerLinter.lean; Mathlib's totient, divisor-sum, iteration, order-bound, and asymptotic definitions.
review.notes: All 13 declarations were reviewed. The source currently records the problem as OPEN; no stale-status issue was found. The standalone sigma_termination declaration was read as the affirmative conjectural variant, with the full yes-or-no question separately stated by sigma_prime_termination. The asymptotic answer slots do constrain their answers; merely allowing weak or tautological candidate answers is not reported as a defect, consistent with CONTRIBUTING.md and the file's explicit note. Neither substantive finding claims an actual nonterminating σ orbit or a basin without density. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without warnings or errors, contains boundary computations for 0–20, and proves the logical and reformulation checks without sorryAx. Erdős Problems and OEIS were read through a public text-rendering proxy after direct requests encountered access challenges; the original book passage was independently read using local OCR. The reviewed file's hash matches the supplied commit. Pre-existing sandbox changes to lakefile.toml and run/ predate this review and were left untouched.

submission.summary: The density statement now requires the basin to have the answer as its natural density, rather than assuming density existence. The σ timing statement now assumes universal termination, and its docstring reflects that conditional question. Also corrected the minor n = 1 exception in the φ-iteration comment without changing that theorem. Only 409.lean was edited; the required compilation succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
